why_us: Posh sells AI assistants to credit unions and community banks, and the BDR is expected to spot an institution in a buying moment, such as a merger or core conversion, and reach it first. I understand that buyer's world better than most career changers: I have run the finances of a practice, built budgets, and worked on reporting and reconciliation. I would be honest that I have not held a BDR role, and the posting asks for two to three years. But I can learn a territory, talk about cost and return with finance people, and keep following up. By chasing underpaid claims I recovered $500K+ in annual revenue.
cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Business Development Representative role at Posh in Boston. I know the posting asks for two to three years as a BDR or SDR, and I have not held a sales title. I am applying because Posh sells to banks and credit unions, and my finance background is directly relevant to the people on the other end of your calls.

For three years I have been the financial manager at AMG Family Dental, running billing, collections and revenue tracking, building the annual operating budget, and reporting variances to ownership. I know how a finance team weighs a vendor: what it costs, what it replaces, and how it will be measured. When your BDR is speaking with a credit union executive about service costs and member experience, I can follow that conversation and keep it practical.

You also want someone who owns a territory and follows through. By pursuing underpaid insurance claims I identified and recovered more than $500K in annual revenue, and I reduced A/R aging by 10% through patient, organized follow-up. At Northrop Grumman I presented cost-saving recommendations to senior leadership, and at FYND in Tokyo I researched AI recruiting tools and presented adoption recommendations to the co-founders. I understand how to explain an AI product to decision makers without hype.

I am a competitive team player, a 2023 Brandeis intramural basketball champion, and a member of the ACYOA executive board. I hold an M.A. in International Economics and Finance from Brandeis and a B.S. in Finance from Suffolk, and I am a U.S. citizen available immediately.

Sincerely,
Alexander Airapetian
